facts.fact: Adwave's article states that 88% of customers read Google reviews to judge the quality of a local business before they commit.
facts.quote: a staggering **88% of customers** read Google reviews to judge the quality of a local business before they commit.

facts.fact: Adwave's article states that Google commands over 57% of all online reviews.
facts.quote: Google commands over **57% of all online reviews** and holds a massive **73% market share** among review platforms

facts.fact: Adwave's article states that Google holds a 73% market share among review platforms.
facts.quote: holds a massive **73% market share** among review platforms, leaving others like Yelp and TripAdvisor far behind.

facts.fact: Adwave's article states that the business description on a Google Business Profile allows 750 characters.
facts.quote: You have **750 characters** for your business description, make them count.

facts.fact: Adwave's article states that the primary category on a Google Business Profile carries the most weight with Google's ranking algorithm.
facts.quote: Your primary category carries the most weight with Google’s ranking algorithm.

facts.fact: Adwave states that campaigns can be started for as little as $50.
facts.quote: You can get campaigns running for as little as **$50**, which completely removes the old financial barriers.

facts.fact: Adwave states that its platform can place a TV spot on over 100 premium channels.
facts.quote: get it on over **100** premium channels.

facts.fact: A third-party analysis by Blogging Wizard of 2 million Google Business Profile pages found that businesses with over 200 Google reviews are significantly more likely to appear in the local pack.
facts.quote: An analysis of **2 million Google Business Profile pages** found that businesses with **over 200 Google reviews** are significantly more likely to land in that coveted local pack.

facts.fact: The article describes big national TV brands as needing six-figure budgets before Adwave's lower-cost offering, which is the article's own characterization rather than a sourced figure.
facts.quote: TV advertising was a game only big national brands with six-figure budgets could play.

facts.fact: The page states that offering incentives for Google reviews is directly against Google's policies, and violations can wipe out all of a business's reviews or suspend its Google Business Profile.
facts.quote: it's directly against Google's policies. Google is all about genuine, unbiased feedback. Offering incentives, sometimes called "review gating," is seen as a way to manipulate your rating.

facts.fact: According to the vendor (Adwave), a business getting 5-10 new reviews every month looks more credible to Google's algorithm than one that receives a sudden burst of 50 reviews in one week.
facts.quote: A business getting 5-10 new reviews every single month looks far more credible to Google's algorithm than a business that gets a suspicious blast of 50 reviews in one week

facts.fact: To report a suspected fake Google review, the page says to click the three dots next to the review on the Google Business Profile and choose "Report review."
facts.quote: Click the three little dots next to it. Choose "Report review" and explain why you're flagging it.
